descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT 3.8; TFA-92597 rule 6 · “Every time-based rule (retention windows, carry-forward, the day roll to Follow-up, "today" on the timeline) uses the server clock.”.

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-07/S28, TC-08/S20

Approach · TC-19 Medication Tracker · S19 A browser two days behind and in another time zone writes the server's date on holds and stamps (both modes)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U23 Server day for the dates the tracker writes: a hold/stop/start tag ('Held · Mon D'), a row's updatedAt and the chart's medicationsUpdatedAt follow the server's day and time, whatever the device clock … (UAT 3.8; TFA-92597 R6 (hold/stop keeps its date))
  • U20 Server clock for the retention clocks: the 18 h label, the 36 h clears and the Nursing Home visit date that drives last-two-visits follow the server clock; … (UAT 3.8; TFA-94699 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U8 Hold/stop dates and reasons are the ones dictated and are kept on every later save; they are never changed to the save date. (UAT TC-19 ER 5; UAT TC-19 ER 10; TFA-92597 R6)

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Local stack; one fresh @roundai.test physician signed in on two Playwright browser contexts against localhost:6473: context A with the real clock, context B with page.clock set to server time - 2 days and timezoneId 'Pacific/Honolulu' (UTC-10); a Hospital patient with lisinopril active and a Nursing Home resident

When On context B: Save & Extract 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' on the Hospital patient, and a pre-round Save Note on the resident. Then open both charts on context A, and read rounding:get / snf:get on the server

Then The Held tag shows the server's day ('Mon D') on both contexts; the row's updatedAt and the chart's medicationsUpdatedAt are within a minute of server time; the resident's newest snfVisitDates entry is the server's day; the row is not cleared or labelled 'not mentioned today' at once on either context

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U23 (not gated: UAT 3.8 + TFA-92597 R6): the Held tag date and the row / chart stamps; a wrong date here is a Fail on the ready-for-qa ticket, and a likely one on main, where mergeMedEventsIntoList and useMedicationEventExtraction stamp new Date() / Date.now() in the browser (day roll is the known TFA-92584). …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S19 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-19.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92597 ready for qa; TFA-94699 in progress

If a phone's date is two days behind, a dictated 'Hold lisinopril' is stamped 'Held · Oct 11', and the next server lifecycle run deletes the lisinopril row, so every device then shows 'No medications recorded.'

Evidence: Allure 2e31b3cf, newspec-c failed, reproduced in 3 runs. mergeMedEventsIntoList and useMedicationEventExtraction stamp with the device clock. This breaks TC-19 U23 (ungated; UAT 3.8) and U1. The resident visit-date part (U20, gated by TFA-94699) is recorded only. The matrix's U23 text predicted device-clock stamping from code reading, but there is no known-gap or ledger entry. Same class as TC-16/S25.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-19 Medication Tracker · Section: A4 · Post-Round · Scenario: TC-19/S19

A browser two days behind and in another time zone writes the server's date on holds and stamps (both modes)

Tickets: TFA-92597 Medication Tracker (ready for qa); TFA-94699 Data Retention & Purge (in progress)

New local lane newspec-c: status failed in newspec-c/results.json → failed (failed (the lane flagged no product issue)).

How it is tested (newspec-c/plan.json, automatable: yes): New Playwright spec: one fresh account, two browser contexts on it. Context B: timezoneId Pacific/Honolulu and clock = server now - 2 days (context.clock.install). Hospital patient with Lisinopril active; ai/parsing:extractMedicationEvents answered at B's socket with a hold event (extractTasks empty) so the stamp, not the model, is under test. B: Encounter 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' -> Save & Extract; B: resident pre-round Save Note (parse answered at the socket). Read rounding:get / snf:get (JWT): row updatedAt, medicationsUpdatedAt within 60 s of server time (time:now), row changeDate / Held tag = server day; resident snfVisitDates newest = server day. Context A (real clock) opens both charts: Held tag shows the server's day on both contexts, row still there. — Browser clock, time zone and a second context are standard Playwright; the server's time comes from the app's own time:now mutation.

Detail:

B18 re-check on 8b4be94a: CHANGED. The data-loss symptom is gone: the hold B wrote is stored as changeDate 'Oct 19' (the server's UTC day; the Tokyo day is Oct 20, both accepted), the row's updatedAt is server time, A and B both show 'Held · Oct 19' and the row is still on the chart after both devices opened it (on e02167f it was stamped two days back and the lifecycle deleted it). Still failing (UAT 3.8): the chart's medicationsUpdatedAt is B's device time, 2026-10-17T18:07 vs server 2026-10-19T18:07 (src/features/rounding/patient/useMedicationEventExtraction.ts:103 new Date()); recorded, gated TFA-94699: the resident's visit date stored as B's day 'Sat Oct 17 2026'. medicationsUpdatedAt feeds the held/stopped 36 h clock (convex/lib/lifecycle.ts chartProcessedAt = max(...)), so a fast device would keep held rows longer; a slow one no longer deletes them. Tripwire: no model call.

Evidence: 3 attached; 1 not attached:

  • newspec-c/rb2-logs/s19.log — .log files are not attached

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (our scripted spec, not written yet): two Playwright contexts on one fresh @roundai.test account, one with page.clock and timezoneId, plus backend reads; its given and runnerGap keep it on the local stack (never ).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
